meta.policy: Shots are data-driven (standards 3.2). Each shot carries a purpose tag, is skippable from the first frame (Skip button + Esc), is captioned, has a text description (audio-description), and a reduced-motion version (still frame + captions). Cinematics never play during an assessment. Total runtime <= 55 s (budget 90 s).
meta.coordinateSystem: Meadow metres: x 0..100 (stream side / wet at low x), z 0..100 (field station gate at x=50, z=-8 outside the fence). y is height above ground.

cinematics.title: Dawn at the meadow
cinematics.effects: dawn lighting + lifting mist (this cinematic only); camera glide; cut to daylight for fieldwork afterwards

captions: 5:40 am. The mist is still lifting off the low ground by the stream.
This is Ashcombe Meadow — one hectare of grass, sedges and herbs.
shots.description: A low dawn sun over a grassy meadow. Thin mist hangs over the wetter ground on the left. The camera glides forward through the gate toward the field station table.

captions: Somewhere out there is the meadow's true answer: how much Butterweed grows here?
You will never count all of it. You will sample — and design that sample well.
shots.description: The camera drifts lower toward a patch of yellow-flowered plants. A field notebook and quadrat frame rest on the station table.

cinematics.title: The reveal — every Butterweed plant
cinematics.effects: camera rises to near-overhead; every Butterweed instance gets a highlight tint; the learner's sampled quadrats stay outlined
cinematics.reducedMotion: static top-down map view with highlights (the same view as the reveal table, no camera flight)

captions: This is every one of the N Butterweed plants in the meadow — the truth you could never see from the ground.
Your quadrats are the outlined squares. Look where they landed — and where they didn't.
shots.description: The camera rises straight up until the whole meadow is visible as a map. Every Butterweed plant lights up as a small yellow marker. The learner's ten quadrats are drawn as white outlines.

captions: Now compare your estimate with the truth on the table.
shots.description: A static overhead view. The reveal table (true vs estimated, per species) is shown beside the map.

cinematics.title: A thousand samples
cinematics.effects: ghost quadrat outlines 'rain' across the meadow in step with the re-sampling simulator building its histogram
cinematics.reducedMotion: chart only (the histogram and its data table appear immediately, no rain animation)

captions: Imagine repeating your fieldwork a thousand times.
Each flash of a square is one virtual sample. The pile they build is the sampling distribution.
shots.description: Seen from above, ghost quadrat sets appear across the meadow one after another — a thousand virtual samples. Beside them, a histogram fills in, centred near the true density for fair designs.
